newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India awards Cochin naphtha to Glencore at -$30/T.
newsitem.headline: India awards Cochin naphtha to Glencore at -$30/T.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has awarded Swiss trader Glencore its tender to sell Cochin high aromatic naphtha (HAN) cargo at around $30 per tonne below U.S. Gulf coast 87-octane gasoline quotes, on a free-on-board (fob) basis, industry sources said on Monday.
Glencore was awarded 30,000-tonnes instead of the 27,000-tonnes initially offered in the tender which closed July 17 and was valid for a day.
The lifting dates for the cargo from the west coast had also been changed earlier to July 31-August 2 from July 27-29.
Glencore had also won IOC's last two tenders for naphtha lifting between July 20-26, also on U.S. related quotes.

The awards, made on July 11, were slightly lower at a discount of $33.75 per tonne for 25,000-tonnes of low aromatic naphtha (LAN) from Bombay on the east coast and of $32.80 for 27,000-tonnes of HAN from Madras pon the east coast.
IOC's last HAN tender from Cochin, offering 30,000-tonnes lifting June 30-July 2, was awarded at a $30-$35 discount to Japanese spot quote on a free-on-board basis.
